parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Describe and explain the variation in the thermal stabilities of the carbonates of the Group 2 elements.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest and explain a reason why sodium carbonate is more stable to heat than magnesium carbonate.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Sodium hydrogencarbonate, $\text{NaHCO}_3$, and potassium hydrogencarbonate, $\text{KHCO}_3$, decompose on heating to produce gases and the solid metal carbonate.
parts.text: Write an equation for the decomposition of $\text{KHCO}_3$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Predict which of $\text{NaHCO}_3$ or $\text{KHCO}_3$ will decompose at the **lower** temperature. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Use the data in the table below, and relevant data from the *Data Booklet*, to calculate the lattice energy, $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}^{\ominus}$, of potassium oxide, $\text{K}_2\text{O(s)}$.

| energy change | value/ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| enthalpy change of atomisation of potassium, $\Delta H_{\text{at}}^{\ominus} \text{K(s)}$ | +89 |
| electron affinity of $\text{O(g)}$ | -141 |
| electron affinity of $\text{O}^{-}\text{(g)}$ | +798 |
| enthalpy change of formation of potassium oxide, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus} \text{K}_2\text{O(s)}$ | -361 |

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State whether the lattice energy of $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ would be more negative, less negative or the same as that of $\text{K}_2\text{O}$. Give reasons for your answer.
